newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand plans to raise $10 billion in loans, bonds.
newsitem.headline: Thailand plans to raise $10 billion in loans, bonds.

text.p: Thailand plans to raise $10 billion through borrowing from international banks and issuing of bonds in foreign markets to build up its reserves, a senior government official said on Tuesday.

Poosana Premanoch, deputy secretary general to the prime minister, told Reuters that the raising of the debt would be made in three tranches. The first would be through the arrangement of loans totalling $5 billion from banks and the remaining $5 billion would be raised through bond issues in two tranches.
Poosana could not give a clear time frame by which the debt would be raised, but believed it could be done by the end of this year.

"It's not that we have a liquidity problem. We just want to keep a credit line available that can be used when needed," he added. The money set to be raised would not be used for spending on government projects, he said.
The decision to borrow the money was made after discussions between Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and the Bank of Thailand last week, Poosana added.
Thailand's public debt as at end-1996 stood at $16.8 billion and the latest borrowing comes at a time when the country is going through its worst economic slump in over a decade.
The baht lost between 15-20 percent of its value after Thai authorities floated the currency last week.

Thailand's finance sector has been hit by overexposure to cash-strapped property firms. The government recently suspended 16 ailing finance firms and ordered them to merge or consolidate with stronger firms.
Analysts said the government needed the extra money because of lower-than-expected tax revenue collections this year due to the current economic downturn.

"We know that the baht flotation will affect economic growth and in terms of tax revenue collection it will result in a greater budget deficit," said Ali Seng, economist at Singapore-based MMS International.
